key_insight: A plug-and-play concept bottleneck framework lets clinicians and researchers intervene at the concept level to distinguish causal from spurious model signals and refine medical imaging models.
clinical_relevance: This could make medical imaging AI easier to debug and more trustworthy by showing which concepts drive predictions and enabling targeted fine-tuning without redesigning the whole model.
method: Align a single-modality image encoder to BioMedCLIP to create a concept bottleneck model.
Use concept interventions to test whether predictions depend on causal or spuriously correlated concepts.
Generate counterfactual examples and use them for expert review and guided fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on a Mayo Clinic ultrasound dataset and the CheXpert 5x200 chest X-ray dataset, where it supported model diagnosis and sometimes improved predictive performance after targeted fine-tuning.
watch_item: Concept interventions depend on high-quality concept definitions and expert validation, so performance may vary if concepts are incomplete, noisy, or not well aligned with the clinical task.
paper_title: Beyond Explanation: Debugging Medical Imaging Models via Concept Intervention
